title: Debt, bonds and fixed-income advice
objectives: Explain yield, duration and credit risk.
body_md:
## Bond basics

- **Coupon**, **face value**, **maturity**, **yield to maturity (YTM)**.
- Price and yield move **opposite**; long duration, bigger moves.
- **Credit rating** shows default risk; **spread** compensates for it.
- **Tax-free bonds, G-secs, SDLs, corporate bonds, T-bills**.

## Choose by horizon

| Need | Tool |
|---|---|
| Parking money | Liquid, overnight, T-bills |
| 1 to 3 years | Short duration funds, bank FDs, corporate bonds |
| Long-term safety | G-secs, PPF, target maturity funds |
| Income | Bonds, SWP from debt funds |

## Cautions

- High yield often means high credit risk.
- Check **liquidity**, call options, **perpetual** bond risks.
- **Hold to maturity** reduces price risk for a single bond; a fund has no maturity.

> **Exam tip:** Yield up, price down; check rating before yield.
example: A 9% corporate bond rated BBB pays much more than a 7% G-sec, but the extra 2% is the market's price for default risk.
